items.title: Edulife Student Carnival
items.registration: Open — no booking required, families are welcome to drop in
items.excerpt: A day of creativity, games, discovery and community.

agenda.item: Stall games and creative activities open
Lunch and family picnic on the grounds

body.text: The annual Student Carnival is our biggest community day of the year. The whole campus opens, the classrooms turn into stalls, and children from both Khagrachari and Luxmichari spend a Saturday making, playing and showing off what they have built.
What happens on the day

The morning begins with a short assembly and a performance led by pupils, then the campus opens up into a set of student-run stalls: games, art tables, a book corner, a science corner, and the ever-popular coding booth where children demonstrate their projects to visitors.

items: Student-run game and craft stalls across the campus.
A project showcase where every class displays its best work.
Refreshments and a family picnic area on the grounds.
A short cultural performance programme in the hall.
Prize giving for class projects and community effort.

body.text: The carnival is the one day of the year when children run the school. That is exactly why it matters.
For families

There is no charge to attend and no booking needed. Bring the family, bring a picnic if you like, and plan to spend a few hours. The campus is fully open and there is a shaded seating area for anyone who needs a rest.

body.title: Volunteering
body.text: Parents and guardians who would like to help run a stall or supervise an activity are very welcome. A note to the school office a week beforehand is all it takes.
Getting there

The carnival is held at the Khagrachari Campus, College Gate. Families from Luxmichari are warmly invited; transport from the Luxmichari Campus is arranged for students, and parents may accompany them.

items.title: Young Speakers Showcase
items.registration: Open — families are welcome to attend; speakers are selected in class
items.excerpt: Students share ideas, stories and perspectives in English.

body.text: Every child in the school speaks. That is the promise behind the Young Speakers Showcase, our termly celebration of spoken English and confident presentation.
What the showcase is

Over one morning, children from every class take the stage in front of their families. Younger pupils deliver short prepared pieces, older pupils give full talks and group presentations. The tone is celebratory rather than competitive; there are no rankings and no winners.

items: Every child in every class speaks at least once.
Pieces are developed in class, in ordinary lesson time.
No memorised scripts beyond what the child has chosen to prepare.
Families are welcome to attend, record and applaud.

body.text: A child who has spoken to a full hall once will never find a classroom audience frightening again.
How children are prepared

Preparation happens entirely inside the school day. Teachers work with each child on pronunciation, pacing and eye contact in short daily sessions in the weeks beforehand. Nothing is set as homework, and families are never asked to rehearse at home.

body.title: For shy speakers
body.text: Children who feel anxious are still included, sometimes as part of a small group rather than alone. The principle is that everyone takes part; the format flexes to make that possible.
Coming along

The showcase is held at the Luxmichari Campus and is open to all Edulife families, including those from Khagrachari, as well as to prospective parents who would like to see the school in action. Refreshments are served afterwards.

items.title: Coding Day
items.registration: Required — places are limited by the number of lab machines
items.excerpt: A hands-on day of building, problem solving and play.

agenda.item: Build session two — free project time

body.text: Coding Day is a whole-day event in the Innovation Lab where children work in small teams on a set challenge and then on something entirely of their own choosing.
The shape of the day
Teams of three are formed across class levels, which is deliberate: older children explain, younger children question, and both learn something they would not have in a single-year group.
The morning challenge

Every team receives the same problem: build something that reacts to what the user does. The solution is entirely open. Some teams build a quiz, others an animation, others a simple game. The constraint is what makes it interesting.

items: Teams of three, mixed across class levels.
One shared morning challenge, with an open solution.
An afternoon of free project time with mentor support.
A presentation to families at the end of the day.

body.text: The hardest part of Coding Day is not the code. It is agreeing, as a team of eight-year-olds, on what to build.
body.cite: Md. Rafiq Hasan, Computer & IT Mentor

body.title: Places are limited
body.text: The lab has a fixed number of machines, so Coding Day is capped and places are allocated in order of registration. Early sign-up is genuinely necessary here.
After the day

Every participant takes home a printed certificate and a short note from the lab team describing what they built, what they found difficult and what they were strongest at. Family members are invited to the final presentations at 1:15 PM.

items.title: Science Discovery Fair
items.registration: Open — no booking required for visitors
items.excerpt: Class projects, experiments and demonstrations for families.

agenda.item: Open viewing and student Q&A at each stand

body.text: The Science Discovery Fair turns the whole ground floor into an exhibition hall. Every class presents experiments, models and demonstrations, and visitors are encouraged to ask questions directly to the children standing beside them.
What visitors will see
Exhibits are chosen and built by the children themselves across the term. Topics come from the curriculum but the framing is entirely up to each class.

items: Working experiments demonstrated live throughout the morning.
Models built from everyday and recycled materials.
Hands-on tables where visitors can try things themselves.
A section on the science behind everyday life at home.
Short student presentations running on the hour.

body.text: A child who has explained their experiment to five strangers over one morning will remember the science for years.
Who it is for
The fair is open to all Edulife families and to prospective parents who would like to see how we teach science. Younger siblings are very welcome; several tables are designed for small hands.

body.title: Please do not correct the children
body.text: If you spot an error in an explanation, ask another question instead of supplying the answer. Getting there themselves is the whole point of the exercise.
Why we hold it in December
By December the term's science work is complete but not yet examined, which makes it the ideal moment to look outward. The fair closes the science term with celebration rather than revision.

items.title: Winter Concert & Art Exhibition
items.registration: Open — families are welcome, seating is first come
items.excerpt: Music, art and celebration to close the academic year.

agenda.item: Art exhibition opens in the main hall

body.text: The Winter Concert and Art Exhibition brings the academic year to a close with an evening of music, artwork and celebration at the Luxmichari Campus.
An evening of two halves

The art exhibition opens first, in the main hall, with work from every class on display. As the evening progresses, attention moves to the stage for the performance programme, with group music items and contributions from each class year.

items: Artwork from every pupil on display, unframed and proud.
Choir and group music items rehearsed in class time.
A short class performance from each year group.
A year-in-review address, and thanks to families.

body.text: This is the one evening of the year when we look backwards, and let the children see how far they have come.
Practical notes

The evening begins promptly at 4:00 PM with the exhibition, so arriving a little early gives you time to see the artwork before the hall fills. Seating is first come, and there is standing room at the back. The evening finishes by around 7:00 PM.

body.title: Bringing family from outside
body.text: Grandparents, relatives and family friends are very welcome. This particular evening is the one most families choose to share with extended family, and we plan the space accordingly.
A thank you

Every member of staff contributes something to this evening, and so do many parents behind the scenes. It is the clearest expression of what the Edulife community is: a group of people who show up for each other's children.

items.title: Parents' Progress Meeting
items.registration: Required — each family books a one-to-one time slot
items.excerpt: One-to-one conversations about each child's progress and goals.

agenda.item: Short talk for families: reading at home
Open floor: questions for the campus heads

body.text: The Parents' Progress Meeting is a morning of scheduled one-to-one conversations. Each family sits down with their child's class teacher to talk through what has been achieved, what comes next and how home and school can work together.
What a slot looks like

Each meeting is fifteen minutes, with a written summary sheet prepared in advance by the class teacher. Nothing is read out cold; the teacher has already gathered the child's work, notes and a short plan for the term ahead.

items: Fifteen minutes with your child's class teacher, by appointment.
A written summary prepared in advance, for you to keep.
Samples of your child's work to look through together.
A short plan for the coming term with clear next steps.

body.text: The most useful thing a parent can bring to this meeting is one honest question they have been holding back.
Held at both campuses
Meetings run simultaneously at Khagrachari and Luxmichari. You attend the campus your child attends. There is no need to travel between sites.

body.title: Booking is required
body.text: Slots are allocated in order of booking, and the morning genuinely fills. Please contact the school office in the weeks beforehand to secure a time that suits your family.
If you cannot attend
Families unable to attend in person can arrange a short phone conversation with the class teacher instead. Please arrange this in advance so the teacher can plan the time properly.
